chunks: And from him, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Musa, from Ya'qub ibn Yazid, from Hammad ibn Isa, from Hariz, from Zurarah, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:

I said, 'I caught the Imam while he was delivering the khutbah.' He said, 'You sit until he finishes his khutbah, then you stand and pray.' I said, 'Is the qada (make-up) part of my prayer the first part or the last part?' He said, 'No, rather the first part, and this is only for this specific prayer.' I said, 'So what part of the fard (obligatory) prayer did I catch with the Imam, and what did I make up?' He said, 'As for what you caught of the fard, it is the first part of your prayer, and what you made up is the last part of it.'

key_terms.أَوَّلُ الصَّلَاة: The first part of the prayer

ai.seo_question: How should one perform the Eid prayer if they arrive after the Imam has finished the khutbah?
ai.summary: In this narration from the *Tahdhib al-Ahkam*, Imam al-Sadiq (AS) clarifies the procedural nuance of joining the Eid prayer late, distinguishing it from other obligatory prayers by assigning the caught portion to the first rak'ah and the make-up to the second. This specific ruling underscores the unique structural integrity of the Eid prayer, where the sequence is strictly maintained relative to the Imam's action, reflecting the jurisprudential precision characteristic of the Imams in handling congregational variations.
